subject: maths
title: Fractions - Halves
introductionText:
Term 2 · Fractions
Fractions — Halves
The Big Idea: A half is one of two equal parts. Sharing fairly between two people gives
each person a half.
Say It Like This
Read aloud
"If I cut this sandwich into two pieces that are exactly the same size, each piece is one
half. If one piece is big and one is small, those are not halves — that isn't fair! Half of 8
grapes: one for you, one for me, one for you, one for me... we each get 4. The word
fraction means equal parts of a whole."
Watch Out For
The slip almost every child makes
"I want the bigger half!" Children (and adults!) say it all the time. Gently: "If one is bigger,
they aren't halves. Halves are always the same size." Let him cut, and let his sister or you
choose first — he'll quickly learn to cut equal parts.
Try It at Home
Game 1 — Fold and check (5 minutes)
Give him a paper napkin, a slice of bread and a sheet of paper. Can he fold each so the
edges match exactly? Open the paper: the fold line cuts it into two halves. Try folding a
different way — corner to corner. Are those halves too?
Game 2 — Two plates (5 minutes)
Put two plates on the table and 10 raisins. He shares them, one on each plate at a time,
until none are left. How many on each? That's half of 10. Try 6, 8, then 7. What happens
with 7?
8 grapes shared: 4 and 4
2 equal parts ✓ NOT halves ✗ half of 8 is 4
Ask which circle shows halves and why the other one doesn't. Then share 8 real grapes onto two plates.
More examples to talk about
• Half of 2 is 1, half of 4 is 2, half of 6 is 3, half of 10 is 5.
• A square can be cut in half in more than one way: straight down, straight across, or
corner to corner.
• Tricky: 7 sweets can't be shared into halves without cutting one sweet in two.
• Tricky: two pieces can be halves even if they look different, as long as they are the same
size — like the two triangles from a square.
• We share things in halves every day: an orange, a sandwich, the sofa.
Key Words
half halves equal fair share whole fraction fold

sourceQuestions.sourceText: Share 8 apples equally between 2 children. Each child gets
A half is one of equal parts.
True or false? "I'll have the bigger half" makes sense.
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: False. Halves are always the same size.

sourceQuestions.sourceText: Draw one line to cut the rectangle in half.
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText:
A line straight down the middle, straight across the middle, or corner to corner — all
make halves.

sourceQuestions.sourceText: Name something at home that you can share in half.
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: Any sensible answer: a sandwich, an orange, a cake, a pack of biscuits.
